title: How Samurai Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the history and culture of the Japanese samurai: their origins as mounted horseback archers, the rise of warrior clans and the Minamoto shogunate, samurai armor and swords (katana, wakizashi, the folding process), bushido code, training, seppuku ritual and the kaishakunin, the Tokugawa peace and decline, the Meiji Restoration and abolition of samurai status, the samurai legacy in WWII and in films. The episode closes with a listener mail segment about a New Zealand place name sent by a nine-year-old listener.

segments.title: Introduction and early samurai origins
segments.summary: Hosts introduce samurai as a topic and discuss their limited prior knowledge. They describe the early wars against the Emishi and Kanto peoples and how samurai grew out of horseback archery (kyudo, the way of the horse and bow).

segments.title: Warrior clans and the rise of the shogunate
segments.summary: The samurai's noble warrior-house status and the bushido code forming from horseback archery traditions. Discussion of the Taira and Minamoto clash, Minamoto no Yoritomo becoming shogun in 1192, and the bakufu military government.

segments.title: Samurai armor and helmets
segments.summary: Description of lamellar armor (yoroi and domaru types), the kabuto helmet and iron masks, and the link to Darth Vader's helmet design.

segments.title: Katana, wakizashi and sword making
segments.summary: The daisho pair of katana and wakizashi, the curved katana blade and its use by horseback swordsmen, and the layered folding technique that produced hard edges on a softer core, with discussion of fold counts.

segments.title: Training, pole arms, guns and bushido teachings
segments.summary: Brutal wooden-sword training methods, use of pole arms, the introduction of matchlock guns from European missionaries in the sixteenth century, and the writing down of bushido in the seventeenth century by Yamamoto Tsunetomo, including tenets such as the lesson of the downpour.

segments.title: Seppuku ritual
segments.summary: Explanation of seppuku (hara-kiri), the ritual steps including death poem and sake, the kaishakunin second who beheads the samurai, the wakizashi or paper fan for those not trusted, and the historical examples including General Nogi in 1912.

segments.title: Tokugawa peace, Perry, and the Meiji Restoration
segments.summary: Tokugawa Ieyasu's control and the two and a half centuries of peace, decline of samurai, Commodore Perry's arrival in 1853, the lesser samurai revolt and Meiji Restoration, the stipends paid in bonds, and the 1876 ban on wearing swords.

segments.title: Samurai legacy and films
segments.summary: Discussion of bushido's revival in World War Two and kamikaze pilots, and a list of samurai-influenced films including The Seven Samurai, The Magnificent Seven, and Ghost Dog.

segments.title: Closing remarks
segments.summary: Hosts point listeners to further samurai material on the site, including ronin and the forty-seven ronin.

segments.title: Listener mail: long place names from New Zealand
segments.summary: Felix, a nine-year-old listener from Wellington, New Zealand, suggests an episode on long place names and shares a Maori place name clip, which the hosts play and praise.
